- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast window (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch momentum — increase forecast slope by 0.1–0.3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if price is above 3σ from 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment strongly supports.
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.3–0.7), model tends to overfit short-term noise — smooth forecast with 3-day moving average filter.
